title: Geometrically reduced fibres near a geometrically reduced generic fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and suppose the generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that for every $y\in V$, the fibre $X_y$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(y)$. No flatness, reducedness of $Y$, Noetherianity, or nonemptiness of the fibres is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-generic-flat-reduced-base-model] to obtain $q:W\to Y$, $g:X_W\to W$, and its generic point $\eta_W$. The base $W$ is integral affine, and $g$ is finite type, flat and locally finitely presented. The supplied residue-field and fibre isomorphisms identify the generic fibre with $X_\eta$ as a scheme over the identified fields; testing on the same field extensions gives geometric reducedness of this generic fibre.

Apply [lem-trf-smooth-open-schematic-generic-density] to $g$. For the specified smooth open $U\subseteq X_W$, this gives injectivity of $\mathcal O_{(X_W)_{\eta_W}}\to(j_{\eta_W})_*\mathcal O_{U_{\eta_W}}$, and geometrically reduced $U_w$ for every $w\in W$. It also gives that every $(X_W)_w$ is finite type over $\kappa(w)$. Every open immersion into $(X_W)_w$, in particular $j_w$, is quasi-compact by the same cited statement.

Apply [lem-trf-schematic-density-generic-fibre-open] to $g$ and $U$. Its finite type and irreducible generic-point hypotheses follow from step 1, and its generic sheaf-injectivity hypothesis is step 2. Obtain a nonempty open $H\subseteq W$ such that $\mathcal O_{(X_W)_w}\to(j_w)_*\mathcal O_{U_w}$ is injective for all $w\in H$.

Fix $w\in H$, put $k=\kappa(w)$, and let $j_w:U_w\hookrightarrow (X_W)_w$ and $p:(X_W)_w\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the fibre structure map. Step 2 makes $j_w$ quasi-compact and its composite with $p$ geometrically reduced. Step 3 makes the kernel of $\mathcal O_{(X_W)_w}\to(j_w)_*\mathcal O_{U_w}$ zero. These are precisely the three hypotheses of [lem-sbc-geometrically-reduced-dominant-descent], applied with $h=j_w$. Hence $p$ is geometrically reduced, including when its source is empty.

proof.text: Set $V=q(H)$. The homeomorphism $q:W\to V_0$ supplied by [lem-trf-generic-flat-reduced-base-model] makes $V$ nonempty and open in $Y$. For $y\in V$, its preimage $w\in H$ has the supplied isomorphisms $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(w)$ and $X_y\simeq(X_W)_w$. Every extension $L/\kappa(y)$ is an extension of $\kappa(w)$ through the inverse field isomorphism; the fibre isomorphism identifies the two base changes to $L$. The latter is reduced by step 4, so $X_y$ is geometrically reduced.
